verdict.rationale: Elastic documents a managed scaling path: Serverless projects autoscale with usage, and search and index tiers scale independently. The serverless docs also imply that self-managed deployments involve managing clusters, nodes and data tiers, and community users report running multi-node clusters via the ECK operator or StatefulSets. However, the pack has no first-party documentation of replication or high availability for self-managed clusters, and a community-cited Jepsen analysis of an older version reports lost documents during network partitions, which tempers confidence. Missing for 10: documented replica/shard replication and HA configuration, self-managed cluster scaling guidance, and evidence of operation at hundreds of millions of documents.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, documented scaling paths — clustering, replication, high availability — carry me from prototype to hundreds of millions of documents

citations.quote: instead of managing clusters, nodes, data tiers, and scaling, you create serverless projects that are fully managed and automatically scaled by Elastic
Separating search and index tiers enables workloads to be scaled independently and reliably, with optimized hardware for each use case.
Serverless scales to your actual usage in real time, so you don't size resources for peak load.
Autoscaled: To meet your performance requirements, the system automatically adjusts to your workloads.
